problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}48 \\ -32\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$

activity_context.topic_title: Dilations and Reflections as Linear Transformations

feedback.problem: What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the matrix $T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Consider the standard basis ${i,j}$ of the Euclidean plane ${R}^{2}$ and the unit square spanned by the vectors, as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14098643/assets/9e322e6ed1ddb8f1d094633e931cd179b7eb9d6f47acd7c7d0809f113df91b22.png)

Now, we compute the images of ${i,j}$ under $T$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{i}^{′} & =T(i)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-i \\ {j}^{′} & =T(j)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following image:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14098643/assets/86adc8f8f32a097b0506adbe15da962e34aad904bf603714bac5cd27712095c8.png)

Therefore, the matrix represents a reflection across the $y$-axis.
